title: Cohomology of a separably closed field vanishes in positive degrees
statement:
Let $L$ be a
separably closed field and
$X=\Spec(L)$. Then every object of the small etale site of $X$ is a
disjoint union of copies of $X$, and for every abelian sheaf $F$ on
$X_{\Et}$,

$$
H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0\qquad(q>0).
$$

Consequently, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, the higher
direct images of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] vanish:
$R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>0$.
(*Source:* this is the case of Stacks Project, Tag
[0EZP](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZP) that is used in this
chapter, namely the case of the spectrum of a separably closed field; the
general statement of that tag, for an integral normal scheme with separably
closed function field, is not needed here.)

proof.text: Let $V\to X$ be an object of the small etale site. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to this etale morphism and the unique point $x$ of $X$. Its fibre $V_x$ is canonically $V$, since $\kappa(x)=L$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ is the identity. The cited statement gives the disjoint union of the open singleton subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$, with each $\kappa(v)/L$ finite separable. By [def-kun-separably-closed] every such extension is trivial over $L$. Thus $V\cong\coprod_{v\in|V|}X$ over $X$. No quasi-compactness or finiteness of the index set is assumed.

For an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ and $V=\coprod_{j\in J}X$, apply the equalizer sheaf axiom of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] to the covering by the components. Distinct components have empty intersection, and each component intersects itself in itself. The empty covering of the empty scheme gives $G(\varnothing)=0$. Consequently every tuple of sections on the components satisfies the matching condition, and restriction gives $G(V)\cong\prod_{j\in J}G(X)$, naturally in $G$. This includes $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 03CN, lemma-abelian-abelian; sheaf axiom applied to the component covering

proof.text: Let $\varphi:G\to H$ be an epimorphism of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and $h\in H(X)$. The local-surjectivity statement [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] supplies a jointly surjective covering $\{V_a\to X\}$ and lifts of $h$ over the $V_a$. Some $V_a$ is nonempty. By step 1 it has a component $X\to V_a$ whose composite with $V_a\to X$ is the identity. Restricting the corresponding lift along this section gives a lift of $h$ in $G(X)$. Hence $\varphi_X$ is surjective. For any $V=\coprod_jX$, choose such a lift separately for each component of a given section in $H(V)$; step 2 glues them to a lift in $G(V)$. Thus $\varphi_V$ is surjective for every object $V$, including the empty object.

The global sections functor is evaluation at $X$ by [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1), kernels and finite limits of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise; evaluation therefore preserves kernels and finite products and is additive. Step 3 shows it sends every epimorphism to a surjective homomorphism. In a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, the first map identifies $A$ with the kernel of $B\to C$, so evaluation gives the kernel of the surjection $B(X)\to C(X)$. The evaluated sequence is short exact. Therefore $\Gamma(X,-)$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian, exactness and vanishing argument specialized to a separably closed field

proof.text: Fix any scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$. For every object $U\to Y$ of $Y_{\Et}$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1) says $W=X\times_YU\to X$ is etale. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(f_*G)(U)=G(W)$ and $(f_*\varphi)_U=\varphi_W$. Step 3 makes this map surjective whenever $\varphi$ is an epimorphism. Such objectwise surjectivity implies local surjectivity using the identity covering, hence $f_*\varphi$ is an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] on $Y$. The sectionwise-kernel statement [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1) also makes $f_*$ preserve kernels and finite products: evaluating either side at $U$ gives the same kernel or product evaluated at $W$. Addition is sectionwise. For a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$, the kernel preservation identifies $f_*A$ with the kernel of $f_*B\to f_*C$, and the latter map is an epimorphism by the preceding lifting argument. Hence $0\to f_*A\to f_*B\to f_*C\to0$ is short exact, and $f_*$ is exact. This argument allows an arbitrary, even infinite, set of components of $W$ and requires no condition on $f$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0EZP, lemma-Rf-star-zero-normal-with-alg-closed-function-field, field case; replace the associated-presheaf computation by exactness of the direct image

proof.text: Take a K-injective resolution $F[0]\to I^\bullet$. Since it is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^q(I^\bullet)=0$ for $q>0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] first to the exact functor $\Gamma(X,-)$ of step 4 and then to the exact functor $f_*$ of step 5. It gives $H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))\cong\Gamma(X,H^q(I^\bullet))=0$ and $H^q(f_*I^\bullet)\cong f_*H^q(I^\bullet)=0$; both functors send the zero object to zero, by their section formulas. The first expression is $H^q(X_{\Et},F)$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and the second is $R^qf_*F$ by the K-injective computation of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This proves both vanishing assertions for every abelian sheaf, without claiming that Tag 0EZP itself states them for arbitrary coefficients.
